key_insight: A mean-flow-skewed turbulent shear layer behaves like a standard planar shear layer plus a decaying orthogonal jet-like component, with coherent structures gradually reorienting toward the planar-shear direction.
engineering_relevance: This implies that misalignment in boundary-layer interactions can materially change mixing, length scales, and coherent-structure dynamics in turbulence modeling and flow-control design.
method: High-fidelity large eddy simulations of a temporally evolving skewed shear layer
Rotated-frame interpretation of the flow into shear-aligned and orthogonal components
Fictitious test cases to isolate the role of mean-flow misalignment
evidence_signal: The abstract reports LES-based numerical evidence showing reduced vertical integral length scale and transient roller realignment, with weak coupling between the two orthogonal mean-flow components.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on temporally evolving numerical cases, so applying them directly to spatially developing or strongly three-dimensional flows may require additional validation.
paper_title: Effects of mean flow skew on turbulent shear layers. Part I. Numerical investigation
